injection_levels.provider_level: Provider or model configuration attached outside the task body.
injection_levels.session_level: Attached to a whole Qwen Code session configuration.
injection_levels.request_level: Attached to one model request body.
injection_levels.content_block_level: Attached to a system, message, tool, or content block.
injection_levels.cache_entry_level: Attached to a cache-control breakpoint or cache entry.
injection_levels.runtime_feedback_level: Reported after provider execution as usage or metrics feedback.

source_classes.provider_config: A provider or Qwen Code generationConfig setting caused or carried the hint.
source_classes.client_supplied: The benchmark client supplied the field before the request boundary.
source_classes.prompt_builder_policy: Qwen Code placed cache-control metadata on stable prompt blocks.
source_classes.provider_automatic: The provider derives the behavior without a client-visible field.
source_classes.pass_through: Qwen Code preserved a configured header or body field at the request boundary.
source_classes.metrics_feedback: The value appears after execution as usage or metrics feedback.

hints.meaning: Carries provider-specific service tier or QoS options through Qwen Code generationConfig.extra_body.
Qwen/provider cache reuse is usually automatic prefix matching, not a literal client cache key.
Carries a static namespace or tenant marker through Qwen Code customHeaders.
hints.supported_consumer: Provider gateway or benchmark capture endpoint

hints.meaning: Carries cache retention through OpenAI-compatible extra_body or Anthropic-style cache_control TTL.
Qwen can emit Anthropic-style ephemeral cache-control markers when cache control is enabled.
Qwen has no native eviction-priority field, but configured body metadata can pass through to a gateway.
Cache feedback is expected as provider usage or metrics, not request-boundary metadata.
hints.supported_consumer: Benchmark report and cache validation tooling

hints.meaning: Qwen/provider paths expose retention or cache control, not a literal pin flag.
